llm.summary: The skill largely does what its name says (social media analysis + AI generation) but contains several incoherent or risky elements — notably committed API keys, undeclared access to files outside the skill, and subprocess/OS operations that are not reflected in the manifest — so proceed with caution.

dimensions.detail: Functionality (analyze/titles/script/product/author/memory) matches the name/description. However the bundle includes a committed scripts/config.js containing apparently live API keys (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY) despite docs instructing the user to configure them and manifest marking config.js as doNotCommitToVcs — this is inconsistent and disproportionate. The Python integration references a separate local skill path in the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...), which is outside the skill's stated directory and not explained in the README/SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning and running configuration and node commands only. The code, however, will: (1) call external APIs (api.deepseek.com, api.tikhub.io) with DeepSeek/TikHub keys (expected for purpose), (2) attempt to launch/drive chrome (and Xvfb) via direct shell commands, (3) run pkill/Xvfb startup commands and exec chrome with DISPLAY injection, and (4) write workflows and invoke another skill's Python script under ~/.openclaw-agent2. The Python script reads a path in the user's home. These file/path accesses and system commands are broader than the SKILL.md's high-level instructions and are not called out as requirements.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only install (git clone + run) — no remote binary downloads or extract steps. That's low-risk in itself. However the code executes system commands (curl, google-chrome, Xvfb, pkill, python), so the runtime will depend on host binaries and perform actions beyond Node.js; those commands are not declared in the manifest's allowed subprocess patterns.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Manifest declares no required env vars and the README asks users to provide TikHub and DeepSeek keys at runtime. Yet the repo includes scripts/config.js with hard-coded tokens (including an sk-... style key). Committing valid-looking API keys is disproportionate and risky (credentials leaked). The keys themselves are relevant to the skill's purpose, but embedding them in the code contradicts best practices and the manifest's doNotCommitToVcs intent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always: false and agentPolicy indicate no forced always-on behavior. However the code will create and write to scripts/memory/ and to agent_data/ paths, and may attempt to invoke or interact with another skill in the user's home directory (~/.openclaw-agent2). The code also executes system-level commands (pkill, Xvfb startup) which can affect other processes. The combination of filesystem writes, cross-skill invocation, and process management is a privilege/impact risk relative to the declared manifest permissions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the advertised marketing features, but has several red flags you should address before installing or using it with real data:

- Do not trust the included scripts/config.js: it contains hard-coded API keys. Treat those as exposed and rotate/revoke them if they are your keys. The presence of committed keys is inconsistent with the README/manifest and likely accidental or negligent.
- Prefer to run this code in a sandboxed environment first (isolated VM or container). The code will execute shell commands (curl, google-chrome, Xvfb, pkill) and can start/kill processes — this can affect your host.
- Confirm the Python integration behavior: cmd_vid_integration.py writes workflows and will attempt to invoke a script at ~/.openclaw-agent2/… which is outside the skill directory. If you don't have that path, the script will return an error; but if you do, it could run other local code. Ensure you understand what that other skill does before permitting interaction.
- Before use: remove the committed config.js, supply your own API keys via the documented config command, and ensure the manifest's declared subprocess/allowed_hosts/ filesystem rules reflect the reality of what the code runs.
- If you plan to allow network access, be aware that prompts/data are sent to api.deepseek.com (AI) and api.tikhub.io (data). Review DeepSeek/TikHub privacy and retention policies for any sensitive content you might send.

If you want, I can extract all locations where external network requests, subprocess calls, or cross-path file accesses occur, so you can review them more closely.
llm.findings:
[hardcoded-credentials] unexpected: scripts/config.js contains literal tokens (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). While the skill legitimately needs API keys, embedding them in the repository contradicts instructions and best practices and exposes credentials.
[child_process-exec-curl] expected: marketing_hub.js uses exec/curl to call DeepSeek API. Subprocess usage to call remote AI endpoints is expected for an integrated tool, but should be declared and constrained in the manifest (allowed_commands/allowed_patterns).
[child_process-exec-chrome-xvfb-pkill] unexpected: The code directly starts/controls Xvfb, pkill, and google-chrome via execSync to perform browser searches. This level of OS manipulation (killing processes, launching X servers) is not described in SKILL.md requirements or the manifest subprocess allowlist and is a higher-risk operation.
[reads-outside-skill-path] unexpected: scripts/cmd_vid_integration.py references ~/.openclaw-agent2/... (another skill's scripts/run_render.py). Reading/executing files in the user's home or other skills is outside the documented read_roots and not explained in the skill docs.
